neighbours.label: the possessive after 'got' in a career biography, where the text is about to say 'start' or 'big break', as against 'got' + possessive for everyday objects and career debuts phrased without 'got'
fire: Long before the Oscars, the director got his start filming local weddings.
The comedian got her start at an open-mic night in Toronto.
Like many country stars, the guitarist got his first break singing in church.
The novelist got her big break when a magazine printed her story.
Before television, the anchor got his start reading news on college radio.
The chef got her start washing dishes in her uncle's diner.
As a teenager, the drummer got his break touring with a local band.
The famous architect got her start designing kitchens for neighbours.
quiet: On a rainy morning, my roommate got his umbrella from the hallway.
After the long hike, the girl got her water bottle out of the bag.
Before leaving the office, the clerk got his keys from the drawer.
At the pharmacy, my aunt got her prescription filled quickly.
Long before the Oscars, the director began filming local weddings.
The comedian first performed at an open-mic night in Toronto.
The novelist was discovered when a magazine printed her story.
The chef started out washing dishes in her uncle's diner.

predictions: fire 0.5-0.95 on ' his'/' her' in biographical 'got his start / got her break'; everyday 'got his keys' and 'began her career' below 0.3
notes: Card: peaks ' his'/' her' after 'got' (got her start in TV, got his Western movie break) plus name pieces (Raz, Alf) and Chinese 开 in 开张. Probe: 'got his start' 0.964, 'got her big break' 0.956, 'got his coat' 0.410, 'got her license' 0.221, 'opened its doors' 0.222. The activation is causal, so the biographical setup before 'got' carries it; near misses either drop the setup (everyday 'got') or drop 'got' (other debut verbs). Name pieces not tested.
